scope: Authoritative cross-area discovery register: ten ranked actions and one unranked hypothesis. Lane reports retain detailed cases and counterevidence. Proposed changes are not implemented in production.
ranking_method: Reproduced loss and control failures first; then source-confirmed release/state risks, documentation/reproduction friction, and human-validation hypotheses. Within a tier: consequence, measured recurrence, confidence, and estimated effort. No participant frequency is inferred from fixtures.
effort_basis: Rough engineering scope, not a delivery commitment: S=1-3 engineering days, M=4-8, L=9-15; excludes recruitment, authenticated-provider access and cross-platform validation.

findings.title: Operation-history capacity disables current Stop and Reply actions
findings.workflow: Control an owned active task after extensive prior use
findings.expected: Historical receipts do not silently consume the capacity needed to stop current work or answer its exact pending request; advertised capabilities match admission.
findings.observed: At 10,000 receipts, interrupt=true and reply=true remain advertised, but both Stop and Decline fail before reaching the provider. A positive control below the limit sends each once.
findings.reproduction: Run reliability/run_reliability.py with the ledger and control-actions cases; repeat ledger using the independent reproduction output.
findings.severity: high: current task control becomes unavailable
findings.frequency: Reproduced twice at the deterministic limit. Incidence in real daily use is unknown.
findings.confidence: high for this limit and native supervisor; authenticated-provider frequency untested
findings.smallest_change: Define bounded receipt generations and safe admission so terminal historical receipts can retire without replaying old operation IDs or abandoning task ownership. Preserve unresolved receipts and exact request controls; expose actual storage failures.
acceptance: Migrate the 9,999/10,000 legacy-receipt fixtures without losing ownership; after explicit reconnect, Stop and exact Decline reach the provider once. Separately, live v2 count/byte rollover preserves exact current turn/request IDs and enables an explicit refreshed action without replay.
Duplicate IDs never execute twice across restart or history retirement; retired IDs receive an explicit non-executing result.
Storage failure and exhausted unresolved capacity fail closed before new work, without a false success or automatic resend.
Capabilities, request identity and UI recovery guidance match the executable admission path.
limitations: Physical ENOSPC, Windows atomic replacement and authenticated control are not tested.
A finite local store cannot promise to return complete receipts forever; the proposed retirement contract is explicit in the implementation brief.

findings.title: Known provider event gaps and unresolved actors lack specific coverage accounting
findings.workflow: Reconnect or reopen after a large burst and inspect past deliveries or delegation
findings.expected: Known provider event loss is disclosed separately from freshness and generic partial history; still-available actor-dependent observations can be reconciled later.
findings.observed: The isolated managed path misses 44/2,744 provider events after 300/3,000 bursts. Generic partial-history warnings remain, but no exact gap is reported. Integrated cold/reopen tests recover persisted parent edges; recent results recover, while results outside the per-thread 64-item tail do not. An unknown-actor adapter input is skipped unless explicitly replayed after roster arrival.
findings.reproduction: Run data/run.py (eight cases), then data/run_dual.py (three source-plus-snapshot cases). Compare native result IDs, persistent spawn edge and provider event sequence ranges against each independent fixture log.
findings.severity: high: known historical evidence can be unavailable without a specific loss explanation
findings.frequency: Two isolated gap cases and two integrated cold-tail cases reproduce loss; one integrated recent-record case recovers. Real provider persistence-shape frequency is unknown.
findings.confidence: high for fixtures and warning gap; medium for how commonly installed providers produce the tested shape
findings.smallest_change: Introduce explicit event-window lineage and structured provider event coverage, plus a bounded deferred-actor queue. Preserve valid recovered facts; do not equate a missing provider event count with lost results or replay user instructions.
acceptance: 300/3,000 isolated bursts report exact missing provider event ranges, preserving two workers and the pending request.
All three integrated cases retain existing recovered edges/results; a provider event gap does not erase valid facts.
A deferred result is applied exactly once when its actor appears; bounded eviction or stream reset produces a truthful loss notice.
Compact and expanded panels expose coverage without hiding current actions; reconciliation produces zero provider mutations.
limitations: General partial-history warnings already exist.
Continuous collectors and persisted spawn metadata can recover facts; this is not universal family loss.
The first change provides truthful coverage and bounded reconciliation, not a full-history archive or guaranteed result backfill.

findings.title: One project's flood removes another project's unread delivery row
findings.workflow: Review a quiet project's delivery after working in a busy project
findings.expected: A bounded notebook shares retention across projects and explains local eviction instead of implying no delivery was recorded.
findings.observed: One result in B followed by 513 messages in A is removed from the global 512-record collaboration ring. B's worker and ordinary text remain, but the Result classification and Deliveries row disappear; Deliveries says no recorded deliveries yet.
findings.reproduction: Run data/run.py retention case. Inspect B before and after the independent A flood and compare the Workboard output with the input log.
findings.severity: high: retained work evidence disappears from a daily review surface
findings.frequency: Deterministic at the reproduced global retention boundary. Real unread-delivery displacement frequency is unknown.
findings.confidence: high for live World retention and rendered empty state
findings.smallest_change: Keep the 512-record budget, evict deterministically from the largest project allocation, and expose bounded per-project loss metadata. Keep reading markers separate from retention.
acceptance: B's one delivery survives 513 messages in A, with total retained records <=512 and a visible A eviction count.
For equal sustained histories from 20 projects, the retained allocations differ by at most one, using the documented deterministic tie-break.
Same-project overflow, more than 512 project windows, restart, late events and duplicates remain bounded and disclose unknown/evicted history.
An empty deliveries list distinguishes no retained results from no results ever observed; source control behavior is unchanged.
limitations: The result's plain text survives in this fixture; this is not proof all copies of content are erased.
The chosen behavior does not retain every unread delivery forever or add persistent transcripts.

findings.title: A pre-send write failure leaves a never-sent instruction labeled Sending
findings.workflow: Submit a task when local intent persistence temporarily fails
findings.expected: If durable intent fails before any provider write, the receipt accurately indicates not sent and permits an explicit safe recovery.
findings.observed: Injected EACCES sends zero provider requests, but a same-ID retry after restoring permissions returns Sending/Awaiting provider acknowledgement until the host is restarted or a new ID is used.
findings.reproduction: Run reliability/run_reliability.py permission case and its independent reproduction. Compare actual provider calls with the receipt after restoring write access.
findings.severity: medium-high: misleading acknowledgement and blocked local recovery
findings.frequency: Reproduced twice with an injected permission failure; real frequency unknown.
findings.confidence: high; provider log proves no dispatch
findings.smallest_change: Make durable intent admission transactional with the in-memory receipt, separating proven pre-dispatch failure from uncertain post-dispatch outcome. Require explicit retry and keep existing no-auto-resend semantics.
acceptance: An injected pre-intent EACCES produces zero provider calls and no receipt claiming to await the provider.
The same ID returns terminal Rejected/Not sent after permissions are restored; a new explicit submission ID dispatches once. No automatic retry is introduced.
Post-send persistence failure and dropped acknowledgements remain uncertain and never automatically replay.
limitations: This fixture injects EACCES; quota testing used EFBIG, not actual disk exhaustion.
Restart is an existing workaround, so this ranks below the current-control and delivery-loss findings.

findings.title: Public container tags advance before smoke verification
findings.workflow: Publish a release that later fails its smoke check
findings.expected: A failed candidate cannot advance supported public release pointers.
findings.observed: The release workflow pushes version/latest image tags before the published-image smoke check. Native release assets depend on that later check.
findings.reproduction: Run reliability/inspect_static.py. Before implementation, rehearse an injected smoke failure in a disposable local registry or workflow stub and inspect tags; do not publish public artifacts.
findings.severity: high potential release failure; runtime consequence not reproduced
findings.frequency: Ordering always exists; frequency of post-push smoke failure unknown.
findings.confidence: high for workflow ordering; consequence untested
findings.smallest_change: Build/test an immutable candidate, then promote public tags and assets only after required checks. Define recovery for partially completed promotion.
acceptance: A deliberately failed candidate leaves version/latest public pointers unchanged in the isolated rehearsal.
The promoted digest equals the tested digest.
Native artifacts and container promotion have an explicit partial-failure status and recovery path.
limitations: No actual registry push, public release, HTTP distribution or signing validation was performed.

findings.title: Windows state replacement removes the old file before replacement
findings.workflow: Recover managed task ownership and operation receipts after a Windows write interruption
findings.expected: Interrupted replacement leaves either the prior valid state or the new valid state, preserving ownership and idempotency information.
findings.observed: The Windows branch explicitly removes the old state path and then renames the replacement; failure between those operations could leave no state file.
findings.reproduction: Use reliability/inspect_static.py for source ordering. On Windows, inject a stop/error between removal and rename using synthetic state; inspect restart behavior without real provider work.
findings.severity: high potential ownership/receipt loss; Windows execution not tested
findings.frequency: Code path confirmed; interruption incidence unknown.
findings.confidence: high for the replacement gap; runtime impact untested
findings.smallest_change: Choose a Windows-native replace/recovery strategy, preserving the prior valid state and permissions until a replacement is durable; test the exact interruption points.
acceptance: At each injected replacement interruption, restart loads a valid old/new state or fails explicitly while retaining recoverable state.
Ownership and duplicate-operation protection survive; no uncertain turn is replayed.
Permissions, antivirus/file-lock interference and running-process behavior are tested on a recorded Windows version.
limitations: No Windows or WSL runtime was available. POSIX replacement passing is not evidence for this branch.

findings.title: Unmatched tool correlation grows without a count or byte bound
findings.workflow: Observe long-lived or incomplete Claude histories with missing tool results
findings.expected: An incomplete source cannot accumulate unlimited correlation state; eviction or lost pairing is disclosed without inventing tool results.
findings.observed: FileCursor.pending_tools retains each unique Bash/Edit/Task start until a matching tool_result or cursor reset/drop. There is no count, byte or age bound. The two-hour fixture emits starts without results; sampled RSS steps correlate with derived per-cursor pending counts crossing HashMap growth thresholds, including about 17.7 to 30.0 MiB near 93 minutes. This is not a heap attribution or a normal paired-tool workload measurement.
findings.reproduction: Read performance/MEMORY-REVIEW.md against the retained soak generator and raw resources.csv. Derive outstanding Edit/Bash IDs independently from writer ticks; compare expected HashMap capacity boundaries with sample intervals. A paired-use/result run remains a separate test.
findings.severity: medium: unbounded retained correlation is possible when source results are missing
findings.frequency: The growth path is exercised by this unpaired fixture. Missing-result frequency and resource use in normal authenticated histories are unknown.
findings.confidence: high for the unbounded map and fixture shape; medium for attribution of the observed RSS steps without heap profiling
findings.smallest_change: Bound pending tool correlation by both entries and retained metadata bytes per cursor, with an aggregate budget across cursors. Retire deterministically, report lost correlation as source coverage, and preserve accurate late-result handling. Choose constants from measured representative records before implementation.
acceptance: Long unpaired streams stay within declared entry, byte and aggregate bounds; all eviction is counted and inspectable as incomplete correlation.
A matching tool result inside the retained window preserves existing behavior and releases its pending entry.
A result arriving after eviction or cursor reset is retained only as supported by its own source facts; it cannot inherit another tool's command, path or success state.
Compare equal-volume paired and unpaired fixtures, recording pending allocation and RSS separately; preserve no-source-mutation behavior and active request semantics.
limitations: The measured fixture never emits tool_result; it must not be represented as typical completed tool traffic.
RSS is sampled and can reflect allocator/OS behavior; no allocation profiler was used.
No production bound or telemetry was implemented in this discovery phase.

findings.title: Current instructions describe older navigation and source contracts
findings.workflow: Connect sources, switch floors, configure the view, or implement a new collector
findings.expected: The documented route reaches the named surface, and authoritative contracts match current source persistence and polling.
findings.observed: PTY inputs confirm c/C open Connections, v opens Advanced, and Tab advances semantic focus. Installation copy describes more direct destinations and floor cycling. Contributor links and Source trait comments also retain old persistence/polling contracts.
findings.reproduction: Follow workflows/DOC_DRIFT.md routes from their stated context; compare source documentation with the current background Poller.
findings.severity: medium: learning and contribution instructions disagree with the product
findings.frequency: Multiple concrete routes/docs differ; participant confusion frequency unknown.
findings.confidence: high for the mismatches, not a novice success-rate claim
findings.smallest_change: Update current instructions and mark superseded design specifications historical; document modal context and observation/control boundaries.
acceptance: A fresh reader follows every changed route at 80x24 using keyboard only and reaches the named surface without unintended actions.
Source persistence and polling ownership have one current referenced contract.
Legacy shortcuts that remain supported are tested before their documentation is removed.
limitations: The first-launch d shortcut was not disproved by testing d in the office; context must remain explicit.
No new contributor or novice documentation session has occurred.

findings.title: Exact audit reproduction depends on ignored local setup
findings.workflow: A contributor reproduces a visual finding from a clean checkout
findings.expected: Evidence includes a complete dependency/bootstrap recipe, with portable alternatives and clear artifact scope.
findings.observed: The exact iteration-6 screenshot recipe references an ignored native toolchain and local Python/font resources. The normal native make check works after prerequisites. Audit evidence accounts for 69.9% of baseline tracked bytes, but network clone cost was not measured.
findings.reproduction: Follow maintenance/MAINTENANCE.md clean-checkout sequence; inspect the screenshot recipe and tracked-file metrics separately from the normal build.
findings.severity: medium-low: reproducibility friction, not application runtime failure
findings.frequency: Exact recipe requires non-tracked resources; real contributor impact unmeasured.
findings.confidence: high for missing recipe prerequisites; low for perceived storage burden
findings.smallest_change: Add a portable audit bootstrap, dependency/font manifest and bounded evidence retention policy for new captures. Keep generated stores/builds ignored and avoid rewriting Git history.
acceptance: A clean checkout can reproduce one full-screen capture and one fixture result with documented commands on a supported host.
Metadata records binary, source, renderer/font and capture method.
Tracked artifacts exclude generated history/toolchains and include only evidence justified by the manifest.
limitations: The 1.81-second clone was local, not a public network measurement.
No broad refactor or Git history rewrite is justified by file size alone.

findings.title: Return context may not match users' reading expectations
findings.workflow: Return to a project after an interruption or on the next workday
findings.expected: Users can recover the prior task and explain which updates they have actually reviewed.
findings.observed: Merely revisiting a floor advances Since your visit even without a record action; the unread delivery remains in Deliveries. Finder reopens with an empty query. No human misunderstanding has been measured.
findings.reproduction: Use the expert Beta/Alpha route in workflows/REPORT.md, then run study task 5 and the three-workday diary with new users.
findings.severity: potential medium; current behavior is not classified as data loss
findings.frequency: Mechanism reproduced; human friction frequency unknown, zero participants.
findings.confidence: high for behavior, low for unmet need
findings.effort: S prototype plus user scheduling; production scope depends on evidence
findings.smallest_change: Test one return-context prototype only if participants miss the next step: retained recent task/search or a clearer visit/unreviewed distinction. Choose the smallest supported change.
acceptance: Record original-context recovery, mistaken reading assumptions and navigation actions before/after using counterbalanced cases.
Proceed on two independent similar breakdowns or one severe mechanism-backed failure; retain counterevidence.
Reject the added UI if the existing visit and delivery model is understood unaided.
limitations: Expert inspection is not participant evidence; text may already have been visible on first return.
The five sessions and voluntary diary have not happened.

findings.title: Character motion and request vocabulary need task-based comprehension evidence
findings.workflow: Recognize a worker, identify attention, and predict the effect of a request action
findings.expected: Identity remains attributable during movement and users distinguish seen, reviewed, approved and acknowledged without assuming invented activity.
findings.observed: Identical-fact captures show moving characters can leave stationary nameplates; compact mode exposes titles/status directly. Seen and Review correctly do not approve. After an explicit reply, one screen pairs no-longer-pending text with a receipt still awaiting provider resolution. These are hypotheses about interpretation, not measured accidental approvals.
findings.reproduction: Use the three same-source presentation conditions and exact-request fixture in workflows/walkthrough.py; then study triage, identity and request-prediction tasks.
findings.severity: potential high if an action is misunderstood; no such participant failure observed
findings.frequency: Expert observations only; zero participant outcomes.
findings.confidence: high for captures and provider call separation, low for human effects
findings.smallest_change: Compare existing tower/compact/reduced-motion views first. Prototype a persistent identity tether or clearer request/receipt wording only for a demonstrated misunderstanding; do not assume more art detail improves comprehension.
acceptance: Measure attention identification within ten seconds and exact request opening within two actions.
Any accidental approval is a critical failure; count recipient/effect prediction errors separately.
Counterbalance view order and record learning effects; measure moving-worker attribution before asking visual preference.
No prototype changes factual states, creates fictional agent messages, or collapses local reading and provider decisions.
limitations: Five participants provide qualitative direction, not certification or a reliable population rate.
Real-terminal painting, assistive technology and authenticated provider actions remain separate untested gates.
